answer: Our guild ties every voting identity to a bonded escrow plus a unique hardware root key, so an operator wanting a thousand votes must run a thousand physical devices and lock collateral on each one. A newcomer's first voyage through the registry costs exactly one bond, and that bond slides to its nadir only when peers prove the device is a virtualized clone. Because forging the quartz-timed entropy fused into each chip is impractical, mass registration becomes a hardware purchase with a shipping delay, not a smart-contract loop.
